title: gRPC and Protobuf Engineering
stage: Engineer typed internal invocation and streaming
centralQuestion: How should typed internal capabilities be modeled and operated when remote calls can fail ambiguously, stream for long periods, and evolve across language boundaries?
responsibility: Design and verify Protobuf schemas and gRPC interactions without pretending that generated stubs turn remote calls into local functions.
incomingBoundary: The Course 6 HTTP API 1.2 and Analysis Events API 1.0 handoff with profiles and migrations through 012.
outgoingBoundary: Analysis RPC API 1.0, gRPC Profile 1.0, proto3 executable baseline, Edition 2024 frontier, migrations 013–015, streaming protocols, method policy, and compatibility evidence.
versionState: HTTP API 1.2 and Events API 1.0 preserved; RPC API 1.0 introduced; proto3 baseline; Edition 2024 frontier; migrations 001–015.
languageStrategy: one primary implementation track plus one comparative reference track

modules.title: RPC Boundaries, Service Ownership, and Interaction Choice
modules.centralQuestion: Which interactions deserve a typed RPC boundary, and which should remain HTTP requests, durable events, or local function calls?
modules.capstoneIncrement: Publish an interaction decision record, service-ownership map, and minimal Analysis RPC surface without splitting the platform prematurely.
learningOutcomes: distinguish local calls, public HTTP operations, durable events, and internal RPCs by ownership, coupling, latency, and failure semantics
recognize when gRPC improves a boundary and when it merely makes a distributed monolith more efficient
design RPC services around stable capabilities rather than database tables or existing classes
separate control-plane commands from event facts and bulk data movement
identify caller, callee, deadline owner, retry owner, and authoritative state for every proposed RPC
reject unjustified service extraction with explicit evidence rather than architectural fashion

modules.title: Protobuf Modeling, Presence, and Semantic Types
modules.centralQuestion: How do we encode domain meaning in Protobuf without allowing language defaults, JSON conventions, or storage models to erase important distinctions?
modules.capstoneIncrement: Complete the Analysis RPC 1.0 message model, publish cross-language presence and integer vectors, and document every field whose absence changes behavior.
learningOutcomes: design request and response messages around application decisions rather than persistence records
distinguish absent, present-with-default, empty, unknown, and inapplicable values
use enum zero values, `optional`, `oneof`, repeated fields, maps, and semantic wrappers deliberately
model resource names, request identifiers, correlation identifiers, revisions, and lease generations as different concepts
protect 64-bit integer meaning across Python, JavaScript, binary Protobuf, and ProtoJSON
maintain a proto3 executable baseline while understanding the Editions 2024 frontier without pretending universal tool support

modules.title: Wire Format, Unknown Fields, and Compatibility Discipline
modules.centralQuestion: How can an RPC contract evolve without corrupting old data, breaking generated clients, or creating behavior that is wire-readable but operationally unsafe?
modules.capstoneIncrement: Publish Analysis RPC compatibility policy 1.0, golden wire fixtures, and a release report that accepts one additive candidate while rejecting unsafe tag, enum, and method-shape changes.
learningOutcomes: explain how field numbers and wire types determine binary compatibility
reserve removed field numbers and names and reject reuse
classify changes across wire, source, JSON, and behavioral dimensions
reason about unknown-field preservation and loss in proxies, stores, and language runtimes
evaluate enum, oneof, map, service, method, and streaming-shape changes
combine local semantic checks, golden bytes, generated-client builds, and Buf compatibility evidence

modules.title: Unary RPCs, Metadata, Status, and Rich Errors
modules.centralQuestion: How should a unary RPC expose success and failure so that generated clients receive stable application meaning rather than transport accidents or leaked internals?
modules.capstoneIncrement: Implement `CreateRun`, `GetRun`, and `CancelRun` with shared status vectors, safe metadata policy, and equivalent Python and TypeScript client behavior.
learningOutcomes: implement thin unary server adapters around application use cases
separate transport metadata from business request fields
map application outcomes to stable gRPC status codes
design safe structured error details without leaking internal state
compose interceptors for authentication, authorization, tracing, and policy without hiding business logic
translate internal gRPC outcomes back to the existing public HTTP Problem Details contract

modules.title: Deadlines, Cancellation, Retries, and Idempotent Calls
modules.centralQuestion: How can callers bound remote work and recover from transient failure without multiplying timeouts or duplicating durable effects?
modules.capstoneIncrement: Implement deadline-aware CreateRun and GetRun clients, persistent retry semantics, deterministic retry vectors, and fault-injection evidence for failures before invocation, before commit, after commit, and during response delivery.
learningOutcomes: derive child RPC budgets from one absolute edge deadline
separate caller cancellation from application rollback
classify transparent and configured retries without assuming all transient statuses are safe
bind mutation retries to durable idempotency records and semantic fingerprints
apply bounded backoff, jitter, attempt limits, and retry throttling
reconcile ambiguous outcomes when a deadline or connection fails after commit

modules.title: Streaming RPCs, Flow Control, and Backpressure
modules.centralQuestion: How do we design long-lived and bulk-transfer RPCs so that slow peers, reconnects, oversized messages, and stale attempts cannot exhaust memory or corrupt state?
modules.capstoneIncrement: Implement `WatchRun`, `UploadDataset`, `DownloadArtifact`, and the worker `Work` stream with shared schedule vectors, bounded buffers, resumable observation, and stale-attempt fencing.
learningOutcomes: choose unary, server-streaming, client-streaming, or bidirectional RPC from interaction semantics
design protocol frames and state machines rather than treating a stream as an unbounded message list
combine HTTP/2 flow control with bounded application queues and backpressure
implement resumable ordered observation without claiming a durable event log
stream large uploads and downloads with exact size, checksum, and cancellation guarantees
keep durable worker leases authoritative when bidirectional sessions disconnect or reconnect

modules.title: Identity, Authorization, mTLS, and Tenant Isolation
modules.centralQuestion: How do internal RPC peers establish workload and delegated user identity, enforce method and resource policy, and protect long-lived streams without treating a private network as trust?
modules.capstoneIncrement: Implement RPC security profile 1.0 with method policy, workload and user identity binding, tenant-isolation vectors, mTLS-ready configuration, and secure worker-stream authorization.
learningOutcomes: distinguish server TLS, mutual TLS workload identity, bearer identity, and delegated end-user context
authenticate callers without trusting arbitrary metadata or network location
enforce method, tenant, resource, field, and attempt-level authorization
bind worker sessions and completions to workload identity and lease generation
protect credentials and authorization context on long-lived streams
produce cross-language security vectors without leaking secrets in status, metadata, logs, reflection, or traces

modules.title: Channels, Health, Discovery, Load Balancing, and Lifecycle
modules.centralQuestion: How do clients and servers manage long-lived channels, instance health, name resolution, load balancing, startup, draining, and shutdown without hiding failure or losing active work?
modules.capstoneIncrement: Implement channel and server lifecycle state machines, standard health semantics, bounded reconnect behavior, two-instance routing evidence, graceful drain, and an operational service configuration.
learningOutcomes: treat channels as long-lived managed resources rather than create-per-call sockets
separate process liveness, service readiness, and standard gRPC health status
reason about name resolution, endpoint changes, load-balancing policy, and connection backoff
configure keepalive, idle behavior, maximum connection age, and wait-for-ready safely
drain unary and streaming RPCs during graceful shutdown
expose reflection and diagnostics according to environment and authorization policy

modules.title: Generation, Testing, Reflection, and Schema Governance
modules.centralQuestion: How do we make proto source, generated code, runtime services, tests, descriptors, reflection, and release policy agree without treating code generation as proof?
modules.capstoneIncrement: Publish a reproducible generation pipeline, checked descriptor inventory, generated-client build matrix, runtime catalogue comparison, and Course 7 RPC release gate.
learningOutcomes: define authoritative proto source and reproducible generation inputs
use `protoc` and Buf as complementary generation, lint, and compatibility tools
build and inspect descriptor sets and runtime reflection inventories
separate semantic unit tests, in-process protocol tests, network conformance, and generated-client tests
detect generated-code drift and unsupported tool capabilities
govern services, methods, owners, consumers, versions, and deprecation through an RPC catalogue

modules.title: HTTP, Events, and gRPC in One Architecture: Release and Final Defense
modules.centralQuestion: How do we introduce an internal RPC control plane without breaking the public HTTP contract, durable event history, database authority, security profile, or rollback path?
modules.capstoneIncrement: Release Analysis RPC API 1.0 behind the unchanged public HTTP API and Event API, execute the final defense, and publish a sanitized service-boundary dossier rather than prematurely splitting the system.
learningOutcomes: assign distinct public, asynchronous, local, and RPC responsibilities in one architecture
migrate an internal call path with shadow, compare, bounded cutover, and rollback
preserve database authority, transactional event publication, and public HTTP conformance
design an RPC release gate spanning schema, generated code, runtime, security, reliability, and performance
reject distributed-monolith boundaries even when the RPC implementation is efficient
produce a service-boundary dossier for Course 8 based on measured ownership and failure evidence
